text: ACARA will work with States and Territories to ensure the Cadetships contribute towards state based senior awards, in the same way as other approved subjects under the National Curriculum
explanation: Administrative arrangement for cadetship recognition within the curriculum; technocratic, no moral language.

explanation: Statement of infrastructure investment enacted; policy/instrumental content with no moral vocabulary.

text: Increased funding for early childhood education by $550 million, or 40 per cent, since 2008.
explanation: Funding statistic for early childhood education; fiscal content per the negative clarification, no moral language.

text: Labor’s Infrastructure Australia is a secretive organisation.
explanation: 'Secretive organisation' is a partisan criticism about transparency/process; 'secretive' functions as a generic negative adjective rather than moral vocabulary (no appeal to a right or democratic duty), so coded 0 per the negative clarification.

text: South Island domestic and industrial users will have their price discounted.
explanation: A pricing policy statement (discounted prices); instrumental, no moral vocabulary.

text: Labor has done little to educate the public on the benefits of cleaner fuels.
explanation: Partisan criticism about public education on cleaner fuels; instrumental/evaluative of competence, not morality.

text: In 1997, a single person on the average industrial wage paid 22% of their income in income tax.
explanation: A tax statistic; purely empirical fiscal information per the negative clarification.

text: Together we're the co-leaders of the Green party
explanation: Descriptive biographical statement about party co-leadership; no evaluative content.

text: without allowing emissions from aviation to undermine our goal of a zero-carbon Britain by 2050.
explanation: Environmental target framing (zero-carbon goal); instrumental/policy language without moral vocabulary.

text: The development of an ‘alternative growth pole’ along the Atlantic Corridor will be pursued.
explanation: Regional development policy statement; technocratic, no moral language.

text: This will be underpinned by new rights for patients.
explanation: Explicit invocation of 'new rights for patients' — 'rights' is listed in the codebook's definition as a moral concept, and the positive examples treat affirmations of rights as moral claims, even when attached to a policy programme.

text: Current investment in developing and protecting the Australian farm sector does not recognise the large contribution farmers make to our economy.
explanation: An economic argument that farm investment fails to recognise farmers' contribution to the economy; the claim is framed instrumentally (economic contribution) rather than as moral desert, per the negative clarification on economic arguments. A mild boundary case due to 'does not recognise... contribution', but the framing is economic.

text: We recognize that adoption costs can be high and in some cases prohibitive for families.
explanation: A factual/instrumental observation about adoption costs being prohibitive; cost framing with no moral-evaluative vocabulary.

text: We will increase access to the arts for young people, particularly those of disadvantaged backgrounds,
explanation: An equality-of-access commitment (arts access for disadvantaged young people) framed purely instrumentally; the negative clarification states such access arguments are 0 unless explicit moral vocabulary is present, and 'disadvantaged backgrounds' is descriptive rather than moral-evaluative.

text: Direct this new spending to health, education, and a few carefully targeted initiatives.
explanation: A neutral spending-allocation instruction (health, education, targeted initiatives). Per the negative clarification, this is a description of funding priorities with no moral-evaluative vocabulary.

text: The Green Party is committed to bringing rail services into public ownership and control.
explanation: A straightforward policy commitment to public ownership of rail services. Instrumental programme language with no appeal to justice, fairness, rights, or virtue, so it falls under the negative clarification for policy instruments.

text: provide direct and meaningful support to land managers in delivering ecoservices; | and
explanation: Instrumental support for land managers delivering ecoservices. 'Meaningful' is a generic positive adjective without moral content, matching the negative clarification's treatment of such descriptors.

text: and providing other services as required, thus contributing to Ireland’s political and economic well being.
explanation: Describes services contributing to political and economic well-being — an instrumental/economic rationale with no moral vocabulary, per the negative clarification.

text: • Conflicting roles and responsibilities.
explanation: A neutral administrative observation about conflicting roles and responsibilities; purely descriptive of governance structures with no evaluative moral language.

text: An SNP government will strive to ensure that Scotland becomes a world leader in securing a sustainable environment
explanation: An aspirational goal (world leader in sustainable environment) lacking moral vocabulary. Under the negative clarification, aspirational visions without moral-evaluative terms are coded 0.

text: With the investment that we are promising in hospital buildings,
explanation: A reference to promised investment in hospital buildings — a funding statement with no moral content.

text: The question that should still be asked of Labor is:
explanation: A rhetorical question set-up aimed at an opponent; no moral-evaluative language present in the fragment.

text: And with new laws to crack down on domestic violence,
explanation: Domestic violence is a morally charged subject, but the text itself is instrumental ('new laws to crack down on') and uses no moral-evaluative vocabulary. The negative clarification covers descriptive references to morally charged subjects framed instrumentally.

text: Fine Gael will support the on-going nationwide roll out of the “Food Dudes” Fruit and Vegetable Promotion programme to all primary schools in Ireland.
explanation: A programme commitment (fruit and vegetable promotion in schools) in purely instrumental terms, like the negative example of the sports programme.

text: Every board shall publish before March of each year an annual report on  its own activities as opposed to the wider work of the state body.
explanation: An administrative reporting requirement for boards; neutral procedural language with no moral content.

text: In particular, as we expand access to talking therapies we expect many more people to recover and be able to seek work again.
explanation: Expanding access to talking therapies is framed instrumentally (recovery and return to work). This matches the negative clarification that equality-of-access arguments framed purely instrumentally are coded 0.

text: and free up  resources  for whānau development.
explanation: Freeing resources for whānau development is instrumental resource-allocation language without moral vocabulary.

text: We will give 1 weeks paid Parental leave for either parent to take, giving them more choice.
explanation: A parental leave policy framed as giving parents 'more choice' — a pragmatic benefit rather than an appeal to freedom as a moral value or to rights. No explicit moral vocabulary.

text: Policy alignment will ensure the wise use of public dollars.
explanation: An efficiency/value-for-money argument ('wise use of public dollars'), which the negative clarification classifies as 0.

text: At £1.4 Trillion, that equates to £54,353 per household;
explanation: A statistical/factual claim converting debt into a per-household figure; purely empirical with no moral evaluation.

text: maintain the Defence Forces’ proud reputation in peacekeeping
explanation: Maintaining the Defence Forces' 'proud reputation' in peacekeeping uses a generic positive adjective ('proud') without moral-evaluative content; it describes reputation management rather than appealing to moral principles, per the negative clarification on generic adjectives.

text: The Nationals are determined to eliminate the divide between those living in and those living outside major capital cities, including any limitation on access to a fair legal system that respects the rights and responsibilities of all Australians.
explanation: Contains explicit moral vocabulary: a 'fair legal system' that 'respects the rights and responsibilities of all Australians', and frames eliminating the regional divide as an imperative. This fits clarification (a) (fair, rights) and (c) (moral wrong to be eliminated).

text: These moves will eliminate remaining inequality in the income tax system and enhance its progressive nature.
explanation: Uses explicit moral vocabulary — 'eliminate remaining inequality' in the tax system. 'Equality/inequality' is listed in clarification (a) as moral vocabulary. Borderline, since tax progressivity is technocratic, but the explicit inequality language meets the codebook's criterion.

text: It is now enshrined in law that we must pay 0.7 per cent of our Gross National Income (GNI) on aid every year.
explanation: Describes a legal requirement to spend 0.7% of GNI on aid. 'Must pay' denotes a statutory obligation, not a moral imperative; the text is descriptive of law, so per the negative clarification it is coded 0.

text: Caroline Lucas and housing In July 2014 Caroline Lucas MP introduced a Housing (Affordability, Supply and Tenant Protection) Bill to highlight the problems faced by private tenants.
explanation: A neutral factual description of an MP introducing a housing bill to 'highlight problems'; descriptive reporting with no moral-evaluative language from the text itself.

text: Support for 2,500 additional aged care beds;
explanation: A funding commitment for aged care beds; a neutral programme/funding item per the negative clarification.

text: Develop new community policing structures, through local policing forums in individual communities, to reconnect the Gardaí and local communities in a spirit of genuine partnership.
explanation: Community policing reform framed as reconnecting police and communities 'in a spirit of genuine partnership' — instrumental institutional design; 'genuine partnership' is aspirational but not moral vocabulary from the codebook's list.

text: We will: save you money by cutting government waste
explanation: Saving money by cutting government waste is an economic/efficiency argument, explicitly the kind coded 0 in the negative clarification.

text: Ireland should be the best place in the world to grow up, and to grow old.
explanation: An aspirational vision ('best place in the world to grow up, and to grow old') lacking moral vocabulary; 'best' is a generic positive adjective, matching the negative clarification's treatment of aspirational visions.

text: Ministerial Cars: We will end the automatic entitlement to a State car for every Government Minister.
explanation: Ending automatic entitlement to ministerial cars is an administrative/perk reform; 'entitlement' here is administrative, not a moral-rights claim. No moral-evaluative language.

text: If you can’t trust Labour and National to go public about poisoned baby milk then what on earth can you trust them on.
explanation: A partisan attack questioning whether the parties can be 'trusted' over poisoned baby milk. Although it touches a morally charged subject, the text is a credibility attack without explicit moral vocabulary (no 'dishonest', 'wrong', 'shameful'). Ambiguous, but under the negative clarification for partisan attacks lacking moral vocabulary, coded 0.

text: All TDs will be entitled to put forward proposals for legislation and a lottery at the start of each session will determine which Bills will be debated.
explanation: A procedural reform (lottery determining which Bills are debated); neutral institutional design with no moral content.

text: We will put in train preparations for the 100th anniversary of the Easter Rising, in a manner that honours the contribution of the men and women of Easter Week,
explanation: Committing to mark the Easter Rising centenary 'in a manner that honours the contribution of the men and women of Easter Week' invokes honour and patriotic remembrance of national forebears — virtue language (patriotism) under clarification (b). Borderline, but 'honours' carries moral-recognition weight beyond a neutral administrative plan.

text: We will support sensible immigration policies that meet our economic needs
explanation: Immigration policy justified by 'economic needs' with 'sensible' as a generic adjective; a pragmatic/economic framing per the negative clarification.

text: Establishing the right accountability framework for schools.
explanation: Establishing the 'right accountability framework' uses 'right' in the sense of correct/appropriate, an administrative design statement with no moral-evaluative content.

text: Republicans share President Bush's understanding that just as events in Europe determined the outcome of the Cold War, events in the broader Middle East will set the course for the victory of free nations in the War on Terror.
explanation: Invokes 'the victory of free nations' in 'the War on Terror' — appeals to freedom as a value and uses vice language ('terror'), both explicitly included in the definition and clarification ('Appeals to freedom/liberty as a value being protected... are included').

text: • there is appropriate time for debate to be conducted.
explanation: Ensuring appropriate time for debate is a neutral procedural arrangement with no moral vocabulary.

text: All recreational fishers should help police the system to ensure that there is no room for poachers and quasi ‘recreational’ fishers who sell or raffle their catches.
explanation: An enforcement appeal against poachers and illegal selling of catches; instrumental rule-enforcement language without moral evaluation.

text: •  Created  2000 jobs  during the recession  through state housing upgrades.
explanation: A statistical achievement claim (2000 jobs created during recession); empirical performance claim per the negative clarification.

text: Constitutional stability for Northern Ireland;
explanation: 'Constitutional stability' is a neutral institutional/political objective without moral-evaluative language.

text: It will dismantle the dysfunctional Health Service Executive (HSE) that was created by Micheál Martin in 2004,
explanation: Dismantling a 'dysfunctional' agency — 'dysfunctional' is a generic negative performance adjective, explicitly the kind without moral content in the negative clarification.

text: conflicts with long-term strategies to cut waste volumes by recycling and reduction, requires huge scale to operate efficiently and generates large volumes of traffic.
explanation: A technical critique of incineration (scale, efficiency, traffic, waste strategy conflict); instrumental/efficiency reasoning with no moral vocabulary.

text: and transition to a prosperous, decarbonized economy.
explanation: 'Transition to a prosperous, decarbonized economy' uses a generic positive adjective ('prosperous') in an economic-aspirational frame; no moral terms per the negative clarification.

text: This will support our aim to make Britain the best place in Europe, and one of the top five worldwide, to do business by 2020.
explanation: An aspirational economic competitiveness target ('best place... to do business'); aspirational vision lacking moral vocabulary.

text: The Nationals believe that, when wealth is generated in a region, a fair share of the resulting government revenue should be returned to that region and to regional Australia more generally.
explanation: Explicit moral vocabulary: a 'fair share' of revenue 'should be returned' to the region that generated the wealth — an appeal to fairness and moral desert, fitting clarification (a) and (d).

text: Half a million of us regularly play sport, while 400,000 volunteer as coaches, match officials and referees.
explanation: Statistical claims about sports participation and volunteering; purely empirical description with no moral-evaluative language.

text: We recognise the contribution that Mäori enterprise and entrepreneurship has made to our nation's economy.
explanation: Recognising Māori enterprise's contribution to the economy is framed instrumentally (economic contribution); 'recognise the contribution' here lacks the moral-evaluative or honour/virtue language that would trigger a 1.

text: We will: Work to secure the full implementation of the Military Covenant in Northern Ireland.
explanation: Working to implement the Military Covenant is a commitment to a policy instrument; the text itself contains no moral vocabulary (no duty, honour, or obligation language), so per the negative clarification it is coded 0.

text: abolish the current 2% limit for funding political parties, which acts against new and smaller parties and could be seen as supporting the status quo;
explanation: Abolishing the 2% party-funding limit is argued structurally (it 'acts against new and smaller parties', 'supporting the status quo') — an implicit disadvantage claim but without explicit moral vocabulary like 'unfair'; hedged ('could be seen as'). Borderline, but coded 0 for lack of explicit moral-evaluative terms.

text: After so long in office, Mr Howard has forgotten what fairness actually means.
explanation: Explicit moral vocabulary: 'Mr Howard has forgotten what fairness actually means' — a direct invocation of fairness as a moral standard the opponent fails, fitting clarification (a).

text: • develop Parents as First Teacher (PAFT) programmes across the country.
explanation: Developing parent-education programmes is a neutral programme commitment with instrumental language only.

text: We will crackdown on overseas producers who don’t cooperate with anti-dumping investigations
explanation: A trade-enforcement pledge (crackdown on non-cooperative overseas producers in anti-dumping investigations); instrumental economic enforcement, no moral vocabulary.

text: Labour will ensure that the Defence  Forces are appropriately equipped and staffed to meet Ireland’s  obligations to United Nations and EU peacekeeping missions.
explanation: Ensuring the Defence Forces are equipped to meet international 'obligations' is instrumental; obligations here are formal commitments to UN/EU missions, not moral imperatives, and no moral-evaluative language is used.

text: Processing of applications and decision-making is subject to long delays, while the absence of legislation means there is frequent resort to the Courts for judicial review.
explanation: A neutral description of administrative problems (delays, legislative gaps, judicial review); factual/institutional diagnosis with no moral-evaluative language.
